name: Excessively dense mobile navigation
summary: On mobile, keep the top area to a title and a few icons, and move secondary controls into a sheet or menu instead of stacking rows above content.
problem: Header, tabs, filter chips and action buttons squeezed into 3 to 4px gaps leave a few lines of content and tiny tap targets. The interface feels anxious and is hard to use.

bad.description: A 360px screen with a header, a tab row, a filter chip row and an action row packed above four list rows.

good.title: Spacing and a filter sheet
good.description: A 56px top bar, one tab row, 20px of space before the content, and filters behind a single icon that opens a sheet.

why: Scrolling is cheap, mis-taps are not. Breathing room keeps tap targets large and the visual rhythm readable.
exceptions: A dense, expert-use tool the user explicitly asked for (a trading terminal, a spreadsheet) may be compact if tap targets stay at least 24px and the density is a deliberate choice.

humanReview: Is there visible space between navigation and primary content?
Can every control be tapped without mis-hits?
